comparator.name: Economics & Society
comparator.sourceNotes: The live Leiden Study Guide confirms a current 180-EC Economics & Society bachelor and publishes the applicable first and second years in full. Year 1 is a 60-EC compulsory foundation in economics, mathematics, statistics, programming and data visualisation, econometrics, politics, law, welfare, institutions and behavioural economics. Year 2 contains 50 EC of compulsory public, international, environmental, labour, migration, inequality and EU economics, Dutch politics, tax law and applied econometrics, plus one 10-EC restricted package in either law or politics. The same official product explicitly states that Year 3 will be included in the 2027-2028 Study Guide. Only the supported 120 EC are retained; the unpublished final year is not inferred.
components: Year 1 compulsory economics, methods and societal foundations

Twelve compulsory modules covering Economics and Society, mathematics, programming and data visualisation, statistics, microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics, politics, law, welfare economics, policy and markets, and behavioural economics.
Year 2 compulsory economics, policy, institutions and methods
Ten compulsory modules covering public, international, environmental, labour, migration, inequality and EU economics, Dutch politics, tax law and applied econometrics.
Year 2 restricted law or politics package
Students choose either European Law plus Social Law or Comparative Politics plus Politics of the European Union.

exception.reason: Leiden is introducing Economics & Society cohort by cohort. The current 2026-2027 Study Guide establishes the complete first and second years but explicitly says that Year 3 will only be included in the 2027-2028 guide. A complete coherent 180-EC pathway for a Fall 2026 entrant therefore cannot yet be reconstructed from current official evidence. Inferring the remaining 60 EC would invent the advanced economics, interdisciplinary, elective and research or thesis requirements.
exception.curriculumContext: The supported curriculum totals 120 EC. Year 1 is a 60-EC compulsory foundation combining economic theory with mathematics, statistics, programming, data visualisation, econometrics, politics, law, welfare, institutions and behavioural economics. Year 2 contains 50 EC of compulsory applied economics, policy, institutions and econometrics plus a 10-EC restricted-choice package in law or politics. The official product confirms that the bachelor as a whole is 180 EC, but its applicable final 60 EC are not yet published.
